entities.name: Rho(D) immune globulin
observations: Routine antenatal prophylaxis is given at about 28 weeks to an Rh(D)-negative, unsensitized pregnant woman.
After delivery, administer within 72 hours when the neonate is Rh(D)-positive or Rh status is unknown; no postpartum dose is needed if the neonate is confirmed Rh(D)-negative.
A standard single-dose 28-week regimen does not require a routine additional antenatal dose before delivery.

entities.name: Rh(D)-negative pregnancy
observations: At 28 weeks, an unsensitized pregnant patient should receive routine antenatal anti-D prophylaxis to prevent maternal alloimmunization.

entities.name: Anti-D timing in pregnancy
observations: For an Rh(D)-negative, antibody-negative woman at 28 weeks, give anti-D now; give postpartum anti-D within 72 hours if the infant is Rh(D)-positive or Rh status is unknown.
The best listed option is D because it includes antenatal administration now and immediate postpartum prophylaxis; postpartum dosing is conditional on neonatal Rh(D) status in actual practice.
